description: The plot illustrates the comparison of accuracy percentages across six different methods as the co-occurrence number increases. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale with major tick marks labeled at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to above 80, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5 units. The plot contains six solid lines, each representing a different method with four data points located approximately at x-values of 3, 30, 300, and 3000. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at an accuracy of approximately 61% and steadily increasing to roughly 67% at the final data point. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning at about 62.5% and rising to approximately 68.5%. The "IKE" method is depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting near 64.5% and increasing to roughly 70%. The "MEND" method is represented by a brown line with diamond markers, which starts at approximately 65.5%, rises to about 73.5% at x=300, and ends at roughly 74%. The "MEMIT" method is shown as a purple line with hexagon markers, beginning near 66% and steadily climbing to approximately 72.5%. Finally, the "ROME" method is illustrated by a green line with square markers, starting at the highest initial value of approximately 72.5%, increasing to about 77.5% at x=300, and remaining steady at 77.5% at the final data point.
